claims.text: What the image looks like Crescent-shaped hyperdensity, CROSSES sutures but not midline → subdural hematoma
claims.quote: Crescent-shaped hyperdensity, CROSSES sutures but not midline Subdural hematoma

claims.text: Example CT: classic crescent-shaped hyperdensity extending across suture lines
claims.quote: Classic crescent-shaped hyperdensity extending across suture lines.

claims.text: Acute SDH on CT: hyperdensity in the subdural space, classically crescent-shaped; degree of midline shift important
claims.quote: CT: Hyperdensity in subdural space, classically crescent-shaped Degree of midline shift important
claims.locator: Common Types of Traumatic Brain Injury table, Acute subdural hematoma

claims.text: A chronic SDH appears hypodense compared with brain; a subacute SDH may be isodense (similar to brain), and an isodense SDH, particularly if bilateral and symmetric, may appear only subtly abnormal
claims.quote: A chronic subdural hematoma appears hypodense compared with brain tissue, whereas a subacute subdural hematoma may have a similar radiopacity as brain tissue (isodense). Isodense subdural hematoma, particularly if bilateral and symmetric, may appear only subtly abnormal.

claims.text: Buzzword: crescentic hyperdensity crossing sutures on head CT → subdural hematoma
claims.quote: Crescentic hyperdensity crossing sutures Head CT Subdural hematoma

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Confirm it is non-contrast (so blood/calcium is not confused with contrast)
claims.quote: Confirm non-contrast (so blood/calcium not confused with contrast).

claims.text: Symmetry: gray-white differentiation, ventricles, sulci, basal cisterns
claims.quote: Symmetry - gray-white differentiation, ventricles, sulci, basal cisterns.

claims.text: Blood: look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH)
claims.quote: Blood - look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH).

claims.text: Brain: gray-white preservation; look for sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift
claims.quote: Brain - gray-white preservation, sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift.

claims.text: Cisterns: basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk
claims.quote: Cisterns - basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk.

claims.text: Ventricles: symmetric size; trapped temporal horn = early hydrocephalus
claims.quote: Ventricles - symmetric size; trapped temporal horn = early hydrocephalus.

claims.text: Bone window: skull fracture, sinuses, mastoids
claims.quote: Bone window - skull fracture, sinuses, mastoids.

claims.text: Signs of mass effect: sulcal effacement, ventricular and cisternal compression, and midline shift; their absence does not exclude increased ICP, and mass effect may be present with normal ICP
claims.quote: Signs of mass effect include sulcal effacement, ventricular and cisternal compression, and midline shift. Absence of these findings does not exclude increased intracranial pressure (ICP), and mass effect may be present with normal ICP.

claims.text: Causes Her chart: bridging veins; elderly, alcoholic, anticoagulated
claims.quote: Subdural hematoma (bridging veins; elderly, alcoholic, anticoagulated)

claims.text: Blood between the dura mater and the arachnoid mater; acute SDH arises from laceration of cortical veins or avulsion of bridging veins between the cortex and dural sinuses
claims.quote: Subdural hematomas are collections of blood between the dura mater and the arachnoid mater. Acute subdural hematomas arise from laceration of cortical veins or avulsion of bridging veins between the cortex and dural sinuses.
claims.locator: Pathology of Traumatic Brain Injury, Hematomas

claims.text: Chronic SDH may appear and cause symptoms gradually over several weeks after trauma; it occurs more often with alcohol use disorder and in older patients (especially those taking antiplatelets or anticoagulants or with brain atrophy)
claims.quote: A chronic subdural hematoma may appear and cause symptoms gradually over several weeks after trauma. Chronic subdural hematomas occur more often in patients with alcohol use disorder and older patients (especially in those taking antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications or in those with brain atrophy).
claims.locator: Pathology of Traumatic Brain Injury, Hematomas

claims.text: Symptoms Acute SDH: usually alterations in orientation, level of arousal and/or cognition; commonly increased ICP even when small; headache, seizures, hemiparesis, symptoms of increased ICP
claims.quote: Acute subdural hematomas are usually associated with alterations in orientation, level of arousal, and/or cognition. They are commonly associated with increased intracranial pressure (ICP) even when small due to underlying cerebral contusions and edema. Symptoms include Headache Seizures Hemiparesis Symptoms of increased ICP

claims.text: Chronic SDH: gradual headache, somnolence, confusion, sometimes with focal deficits or seizures
claims.quote: Gradual headache, somnolence, confusion, sometimes with focal deficits or seizures
claims.locator: Common Types of Traumatic Brain Injury table, Chronic subdural hematoma

claims.text: Older patients may consider the head injury relatively trivial or may have even forgotten it
claims.quote: Older patients may consider the head injury relatively trivial or may have even forgotten it.
claims.locator: Pathology of Traumatic Brain Injury, Hematomas

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: evacuation if symptomatic / >10 mm thick / >5 mm midline shift
claims.quote: Evacuation if symptomatic / >10 mm thick / >5 mm midline shift

claims.text: A midline shift of > 5 mm is generally considered an indication for surgical evacuation of the hematoma
claims.quote: A shift of > 5 mm from the midline is generally considered to be an indication for surgical evacuation of the hematoma.

claims.text: Factors that suggest a need for emergent surgery: midline brain shift of > 5 mm, compression of the basal cisterns, worsening neurologic examination findings
claims.quote: Factors that suggest a need for emergent surgery include Midline brain shift of > 5 mm Compression of the basal cisterns Worsening neurologic examination findings

claims.text: Intracranial hematomas may require urgent surgical evacuation to prevent or treat brain shift, compression and herniation, so early neurosurgical consultation is mandatory
claims.quote: Intracranial hematomas may require urgent surgical evacuation to prevent or treat brain shift, compression, and herniation; hence, early neurosurgical consultation is mandatory.

claims.text: Patients with small subdural hematomas can often be treated without surgery
claims.quote: Patients with small subdural hematomas can often be treated without surgery.

claims.text: Chronic SDH may require surgical drainage, but much less urgently than acute SDH
claims.quote: Chronic subdural hematomas may require surgical drainage but much less urgently than acute subdural hematomas.
